source_caption_text:
7 years ago today, $tupid Young dropped his album “True Story II,” a project that helped further establish the Long Beach rapper as a serious name in the rap game. 🔥🇰🇭

Released in September 2019 through Afficials / EMPIRE, True Story II was a 14-track project that showed how far $tupid Young had come since breaking through with records like “Mando” with Mozzy. The album brought together artists from different corners of hip-hop, including Fenix Flexin, YBN Nahmir, Smokepurpp, E-40, Iamsu!, Pacman Da Gunman, Azjah and more.

The project featured $tupid Young working with both established West Coast names and some of the biggest young artists in rap at the time. “What I Want” with Fenix Flexin, “Glocc in My Pants” with YBN Nahmir, “Late Night Trap” with Smokepurpp and “All Day” with Bay Area legend E-40 gave the album a wide range of sounds while still keeping Young’s signature West Coast style at the center.

One of the standout records from the album was “Lights Out,” which eventually received its own music video and has become one of $tupid Young’s most recognizable videos. The video is now sitting at 16 million+ views on YouTube, showing the lasting popularity of the record seven years after the album originally dropped.

True Story II arrived during an important stretch of $tupid Young’s career. He was no longer simply an underground Long Beach artist — he was building relationships with artists across California and beyond while continuing to bring his Cambodian-American identity and Long Beach roots into mainstream hip-hop spaces.

Seven years later, True Story II remains an important part of $tupid Young’s catalog and a snapshot of where he was during one of the biggest periods of his career.
